audit.why: 8/10 HARD holds at 50.38% over 264 games: Brand out-ranges him before 6 (Q 1050 / W 900 vs Avengerang 850 and auto range), then loses control once Comeuppance and camouflage let Akshan pick the moment.

audit.whatIsWrong: All seven chart rows disagreed across layers — full said Akshan 0-6, content and packet said Brand 0-6 — and the full-layer whys described Brand winning under Akshan verdicts.
audit.why: Before 6 Akshan's only ranged tool is Avengerang (850, 9s at rank 1) and he must walk to auto range, so Brand's 900/1050 poke owns 1-5. From 6 Comeuppance locks on at 2500 range and scales with missing health — the poke trades Brand wins are the setup for it — and Going Rogue is camouflage on an approach, so Akshan picks the fight from there.
audit.corrected: Rows 0-3 -> Brand (full side + rating; content win[0..3] already Brand). Rows 4-6 -> Akshan (full side already Akshan; content win[4..6] moved), with every why on both layers rewritten. Proposed as one atomic chart group.

audit.whatIsWrong: The shield interaction was missing entirely, and breakdown.cooldowns had no digit in it (lint) despite the packet flagging 'NO cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere'.
audit.why: Dirty Fighting shields Akshan on every third hit from his attacks and abilities, so a burst window opened into a fresh shield is wasted — it must be baited out first. Heroic Swing runs 18s at rank 1 down to 12s at rank 5, Avengerang 9s down to 5s, Comeuppance 100/85/70: those are the windows the page never gave the reader.
audit.corrected: Shield stated in dontsFull[0].d and dontsFull[2].d; real cooldowns and explicit 'wait for X before Y' sequencing written into breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: report[8] told the reader to buy anti-heal 'into his sustain'.
audit.why: Akshan's Dirty Fighting grants a shield, not healing — Grievous Wounds does nothing to it.
audit.corrected: Replaced with the Rylai's slow line, which actually keeps him out of Heroic Swing range.

edits.before: Comeuppance gives Akshan a global execute threat, but it's a channel he has to commit to, and your Conflagration/Blaze combo punishes him hard if he ever walks in to land the setup.
edits.after: Comeuppance locks on from 2500 range on a 100s cooldown and scales with your missing health, so every poke trade you take at half HP is him storing bullets you already paid for.

edits.before: Even with Comeuppance online at 6, the ult is a long channel that telegraphs itself, and closing distance to actually threaten you with autos walks him straight into your Blaze zone, so your lane lead only grows through this stretch.
edits.after: Comeuppance at 6 does not need him to close: it locks on from 2500 range and scales with your missing health, so a chipped Brand is the setup. Shove with W-E, hold E-Q for the Heroic Swing entry, and recall on a crash instead of sitting low.

edits.before: Your poke and AoE zoning continue to outclass his single-target auto-reliant kit in skirmishes, though his Heroic Swing repositioning and stealth off takedowns means you keep vision up and don't overextend alone into his pick angles.
edits.after: Heroic Swing repositioning and camouflage off takedowns let him choose the angle, and an immobile mage standing alone is the easiest angle there is. Fight inside your team, keep control wards on both flanks, and hold Pyroclasm for the clump he swings into.

edits.before: Liandry's onward, force the extended exchanges: every rotation is percent-health math and every river clump is a Pyroclasm invoice.
edits.after: Post-6, stop trading at low HP: Comeuppance scales with missing health from 2500 range. Shove with W-E and recall on the crash.

edits.before: - Akshan Heroic Swing: matchup-defining — His swing engage/escape — fight only while it is down. Check it before every step-up. - E-Q stun package is the lifeline; chip damage never gets it. - The ult answers fights, not waves.
edits.after: - Heroic Swing is 18s at rank 1 and 12s at rank 5 — step up in that window, not into it. - Avengerang is 9s at rank 1; once it is out you can walk the wave. - Comeuppance is 100s at 6 — after he spends it, your E-Q package outlasts him.

edits.before: Carry through AoE math — no burst mage damages three targets like Brand; your job is the spacing that lets the bounces vote.
edits.after: Carry by punishing the swing — E-Q on his Heroic Swing landing plus Pyroclasm's slow strands him inside your team.

edits.before: You are the detonator: spread Blaze with E-W, R the clump, and watch the bounces win the objective fight your team merely attended.
edits.after: Fight inside your frontline: he swings in for the immobile target. Spread Blaze with E-W, R the clump, and ward both flank entries.

edits.before: E the instant ablaze, Q the stun, W the stunned body, walk — the full package chunks half a bar and the burn writes the receipt.
edits.after: Going Rogue is camouflage on a 5500-range approach — a control ward on the flank is the only thing that makes his entry a fair fight.

edits.before: Akshan spends Heroic Swing early — the closest thing this matchup has to a guarantee.
edits.after: Pyroclasm bounces and slows ablaze targets — 100s at rank 1, spend it when he swings in.

edits.before: That is Akshan’s rehearsed moment — don’t audition for it.

edits.before: W-poking on cooldown with Q unbanked while his engage is loaded — Brand without the stun threat is a bonfire waiting for company.
edits.after: Every third hit from Akshan grants a shield, so a W thrown into a fresh shield window buys him the trade and costs you the stun.
